subject: MediCorp SIG: follow-up on logs, retention, and model-training commitments
messages:
From: Amanda Liu <amanda.liu@medicorp.com>
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: compliance@medicorp.com
Date: 2027-04-10T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: SIG follow-ups: logs, retention & training on customer content

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for the responses your team submitted to our SIG inventory. A couple of our reviewers asked for clarification on 3 items that are blocking our internal sign-off:

1) Prompt/response logs: your answer indicates logs are "retained per customer policy." Can you confirm the default retention length for request/response bodies in Redwood's hosted offering, and whether there's an option to set it to 0 (no retention) for enterprise customers?

2) KV / cache persistence: we need explicit confirmation whether any in-flight KV or cache (used to speed generation) is ever written to durable storage or backups. Our security team requires concrete wording for the SIG.

3) Training on customer data: we saw the checkbox that Redwood does not use customer content to train models by default. Can you provide the exact contractual commitment/exception text you offer for customers who opt-in to improvements, and typical redaction/aggregation controls you apply?

We are trying to finalize the SIG this week; can you get back with short, concrete answers and any supporting exhibits (one-page summary or policy excerpt) we can attach to the questionnaire?

Thanks,
Amanda
Amanda Liu
Senior Manager, Security & Privacy
MediCorp Health

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Amanda Liu <amanda.liu@medicorp.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, soojin.lee@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-11T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-ups: logs, retention & training on customer content

Amanda — thanks for the clear list. Short answers here, attaching a one-page retention summary. See more detail below and I can route legal if you want contractual language.

1) Prompt/response logs: Hosted (default) retention is 14 days for full request/response bodies (used for debugging, rate-limit abuse, and safety monitoring). We offer a dedicated option for enterprise customers to reduce this to 0 days (no persistent storage of request/response bodies) or to a custom retention window as part of Dedicated/Private contracts.

2) KV / cache persistence: Runtime KV caches are held in-memory on serving nodes and are not persisted to durable disk; they are not included in backups or object storage. When a node is terminated the in-memory cache is discarded. We never snapshot KV caches to persistent logs.

3) Training on customer data: By default Redwood does not use customer prompts or responses to train or fine-tune base models. Customers may opt-in explicitly via contract or console setting to share anonymized telemetry for aggregate model quality improvements. Any opt-in is governed by a documented annex that: (a) excludes personally identifiable information per customer redaction rules, (b) only collects aggregated gradients/metrics or sampled anonymized text, and (c) can be revoked with 30 days' notice.

Attached: redwood-retention-summary-20270411.pdf (one-page explainer). If you need formal language to put into the SIG 'exception/notes' field, we can provide a short paragraph from Legal.

Would you like us to add a sentence to the SIG that enterprise customers can choose 0-day retention and opt-out of telemetry? If so I'll loop in Marissa to draft exact wording.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive — Strategic Customers
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: connor.obrien@redwood.ai, soojin.lee@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-11T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-ups: logs, retention & training on customer content

Amanda — looping in Legal. Below is a succinct paragraph we can drop into the SIG 'notes' field and into the contractual security exhibit. Feel free to paste directly.

"Redwood Inference retention and training commitments: By default, Redwood retains request and response bodies in hosted environments for 14 days for operational troubleshooting, abuse detection, and safety monitoring. For enterprise customers (Dedicated or Private deployments) Redwood will implement a mutually-agreed retention policy, including the option for 0-day retention (no persistent storage of request/response bodies). Runtime key-value caching used to accelerate inference is in-memory only and is not persisted to durable storage or included in backups. Redwood does not use customer-provided prompts, responses, or other customer content to train or update production models unless the customer provides explicit, documented opt-in consent via contract and console controls; any opt-in is limited to aggregated or redacted telemetry and may be revoked by the customer with 30 days' notice."

If you want this as a PDF exhibit we can produce a short signed attestation. Also attaching a draft of the training-commitment text in case your procurement wants the exact clause.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

Dylan / Marissa — this is great, thanks for the quick turnaround. The paragraph Marissa drafted is exactly what our reviewers needed. Two quick follow-ups:

- Can you confirm whether the 14-day default applies to both hosted single-tenant and multi-tenant deployments? (we assume multi-tenant hosted only; Dedicated customers typically get contractual options).
- For the opt-in telemetry, can you provide a short description of the redaction steps you run (PII heuristics, token removal, regex filters) so our privacy engineers can assess residual risk?

If it's easier to close this over a 20-minute call, I'm available tomorrow morning PST. Otherwise we can attach the drafted paragraph and the one-page summary to the SIG and finish the questionnaire today.

Thanks again,
Amanda
